catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds a syringe plunger position: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 binds robot.arm/motion.axis and takes joint positions in rad, while this device moves a plunger to an encoder step between 0 and 3000. The bound is stated by the upstream validation (tecancavro/models.py:478).

cap.fluid.dispense.v1 binds lab.liquid_handler/lab.pipette and needs a target {labware, well}; this pump dispenses from a numbered distribution-valve port and knows no labware. cap.actuation.pump.v1 binds fluid.pump but requires a flow_rate/direction pair, while the pump sets its rate with an OEM speed code and start/top/cutoff speeds in pulses/s, not with a flow rate in uL/s.

cap.motion.stop.v1 binds robot.arm/robot.mobile_base/motion.axis. This device stops by sending the OEM T command (terminateCmd) to a syringe pump; the action is also the safe_state action SAFE-045 asks of an R2 hardware driver without a documented hardware e-stop.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card says family serial / helper SerialDriver. The upstream does not speak text lines: TecanAPI wraps every command in the Tecan OEM API frame (STX 0x02, address, sequence byte, command payload, ETX 0x03 and an XOR checksum; tecancavro/tecanapi.py:87-91) and XCaliburD builds each payload from parts ('S{code}', 'v{speed}', 'V{speed}', 'c{speed}', 'L{slope}', 'A{position}', 'P{steps}', 'O{port}'; tecancavro/models.py:453-565), so a command table cannot reproduce the bytes (driver-authoring.md, 'Choosing the shape'). The package is therefore a direct Driver over tecancavro.models:XCaliburD with a native.py factory. The card's candidate classes were checked with catalog show: cap.fluid.dispense.v1 binds lab.liquid_handler/lab.pipette, and cap.motion.joint_position.v1 and cap.motion.stop.v1 bind robot.arm/motion.axis, so none binds device_kind fluid.pump; cap.actuation.pump.v1 does bind it but requires a flow_rate/direction pair, which this pump does not have (its rate is an OEM speed code plus start/top/cutoff speeds in pulses/s), so the actions are extensions with catalogue_requests. NOT COVERED: the hardware backend was never opened (no pump, no serial port) and reviewed_by stays null, so this package is checked on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The fake models the upstream command chain (queue, executeChain, terminateCmd) and the 0-3000 plunger travel, but it does not model the frame bytes, the SPEED_CODES table (a speed code is stored as its own number, not converted to pulses/s) or the pump timing; nothing ran against hardware. G4.REF_VALUE warnings (2), explained in facts.md: the port bound 1..9 cites tecancavro/models.py:441-443, which shows the '0 < to_port <= num_ports' test and the 'between 1 and' message but not the default 9 (num_ports=9 on models.py:80); the volume bound 0..1000 uL cites the step conversion on models.py:866, and the 1000 uL syringe default is on models.py:42. The clone's only manual is a PDF (docs/Tecan_Cavro_XCALIBUR_Manual.pdf); no page of it was read, so none is cited. The e-stop and the safe-state action x-cap.benpruitt.stop.v1 both call the native terminateCmd(); no text of the clone documents an independent hardware e-stop, so SAFE-045 is met by the safe-state action. check-report.json is generated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-29; reviewed_by stays null): accepted after reviewer edits. The dispense port bound (1 to 9) and volume bound (0 to 1000 uL) came from constructor defaults (num_ports, syringe_ul) and are now Limit.operator_required; site-limits.example.json, facts.md and the test cases follow. The DEVIATION FROM THE CARD is accepted: a registry override now makes the card a direct driver. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
